data.content_ref: inline:Self-applicability: the extension mechanism is itself governed by the same skeptical fixed point. Candidate extensions are nodes in a meta-framework; an extension is accepted only if it survives the Pass 1 rules applied to that meta-framework, where attacks are 'violates guarantee G' and defenses are 'preserves G by argument A'. This makes the semantics closed under its own acceptance policy — no extension can be adopted that would not itself be IN in the grounded extension of the meta-framework. Open question: does the meta-fixpoint reach a fixed point in one level (idempotence), or does it oscillate or require transfinite iteration — and does idempotence itself decide which extensions are legitimate?
